recipe.literal: The cluster before les has a broad U-like lower bowl, a tall right stem, a diagonal triangular crossing through its upper-right area and a short low return hook. Their intersections do not isolate a separate cancellation stroke. Once-viewed crop: readers/025/A/crops/08_crossed_U_Sigma.png. Complete selected states in source order: \deleted{U\Sigma} | \deleted{\bigcup\Sigma} | \deleted{U} | U\Sigma | \text{et}. All original three cancelled candidates and both whole live states remain in this source order. Their intersections leave cancellation/live state unresolved, his hand. The following live les stays outside the group.

The next Sigma has a short heavy detached upper run, a separate lower descending entry, a sharp middle turn and a low foot that touches the alpha at its right end. The alpha rises into a short curl and returns through a small lower loop to a rightward tail. The plus is a separate dark cross. Once-viewed crop: readers/025/A/crops/08_crossed_U_Sigma.png. Complete selected states in source order: \Sigma_\alpha^+ with detached head/retrace | \Sigma_\alpha^+ with independent upper run. The single shared body-foot/alpha path, separate plus and upper run are retained once. The body and attached alpha are his hand; the independent-upper-run candidate alone retains undetermined upper-run hand. The original source prints the later primary unmarked under S01, while both local states remain recorded.

The lower K has its tall stem and two right branches still visible through a folded, looped cancellation that descends beyond the lower right branch. Above-left is a separate clear K, set-minus, opening brace, dotted i and closing brace. A much thinner long run starts low-left of the deleted K, curves upward through its upper area, continues diagonally up-right and ends in a small hooked turn. Its guide versus extended-cancellation role remains open from these crossings. Once-viewed crop: readers/025/A/crops/10_K_replacement.png. Complete selected states in source order: \deleted{K}\inserted{K\setminus\{i\}} with long run acting as guide | \deleted{K}\inserted{K\setminus\{i\}} with long run acting as strike. The deleted K and raised inserted K\setminus\{i\} are firm. A025-M02 owns the long curved run once, with guide/strike role low confidence and his-hand attribution. The parent owns the K forms and looped cancellation. Live et les remains outside.

The prose Sigma has a pale left tip leading into a dark upper horizontal, separated by a visible white band from the lower diagonal entry. Its sharp middle turn leads down-left to a straight low foot. The alpha sits separately below-right of that foot, with a low oval loop, rising branch and short descending right tail. The plus is a separate short cross. Once-viewed crop: readers/025/A/crops/11_prose_sigma.png. Complete selected states in source order: \Sigma_\alpha^+ with detached head/retrace | \Sigma_\alpha^+ with independent upper run. Main body, alpha and plus are his hand; only the independent-upper-run candidate has undetermined upper-run hand. The exact later primary remains unmarked under S01. The full parenthetical (\alpha\in K\setminus\{i\}) stays outside the glyph group.

The participle begins with a looped d, low e and tall t; no distinct initial acute is visible over that first e. The remaining letter bodies support determinés/determines. Over the word's final area, the q from que on the preceding line descends in a very long thin stroke ending with a small bend. A separate short oblique stroke sits just below-left of that endpoint and above the final e/s area. Its attribution to a final acute or to the descending q's terminal trace remains unresolved. Once-viewed crop: readers/025/A/crops/12_determines.png. \unsure{determinés|determines}, in that order. The initial e carries no acute in either selected candidate. The short oblique stroke near the ending retains final-acute versus preceding-q-terminal-trace attribution; the complete preceding que descender stays in the evidence and attachment scope. The whole word remains qualified, his hand.

The first lower Sigma has a tiny initial dark head piece, a small visible gap, and then a long shallow rising head run. The body starts below that run, curves through the middle and returns to a long rising low foot with a downward right hook. A separate plus is clear. Its index is only a short bent dark stroke, with no separate dot. Once-viewed crop: readers/025/C/14_lower_sigmas.png. Complete selected states in source order: \Sigma_i^+ with detached head/retrace | \Sigma_{\prime}^+ with detached head/retrace | \Sigma_i^+ with independent upper run | \Sigma_{\prime}^+ with independent upper run. The tiny first head piece, intervening gap, long head run, body, plus and single short index are preserved. Main body/index/plus is his hand; only the independent-upper-run candidate retains undetermined upper-run hand. The exact later primary remains unmarked under S01; i.e. stays outside.

The second lower Sigma has a detached upper run with a paler left entry, a separate body curving through the middle, and a low foot that bends downward at its right end. Its upper minus is a thick separate horizontal. Its index is a single short near-vertical dark stroke, with no separate dot. Once-viewed crop: readers/025/C/14_lower_sigmas.png. Complete selected states in source order: \Sigma_i^- with detached head/retrace | \Sigma_{\prime}^- with detached head/retrace | \Sigma_i^- with independent upper run | \Sigma_{\prime}^- with independent upper run. The detached head with pale left entry, body, minus and single undotted short index are preserved. Main glyph is his hand; only the independent-upper-run candidate retains undetermined upper-run hand. The exact later primary remains unmarked under S01; the following sentence point stays outside.

The final que has an open q loop, a very long descending stem ending in a short left foot, and joined low u/e strokes ending in a downward right hook. A separate small dark triangular point lies to the right of the upper portion of the descender, with clear white separation from the letters. Once-viewed crop: readers/025/B/15_que_adjacent_point.png. Complete que with its open q loop, full long descender, joined u/e and one separate triangular point to the right of the descender, through exact B025-G09. Je dis precedes outside the group. The word is firm, his hand; only the separate point retains unresolved hand, role, attachment and surface origin. The whole source group keeps its original qualifier.

A faint upper curved run bends rightward and down, then continues through a paler middle section. Below it, a darker slant descends left into a short nearly horizontal foot. A still farther-left short pale foot segment is separated from that low run by a light gap. Once-viewed crop: readers/025/B/14_lower_curve.png. Complete faint lower-sheet curve through B025-M01, with all four components: upper curved run, pale middle continuation, lower diagonal/foot, and detached short left foot. Its exact B outer placement is retained. Hand, role, attachment and surface origin remain undetermined; no character is assigned.

Two separate dark rounded-angular points lie in the lower-right blank area. The upper one is to the right of the lower one, with a clear intervening gap. Once-viewed crop: readers/025/A/crops/15_lower_points.png. Complete pair of separate dark rounded-angular lower-right points through B025-M02, the upper point to the right of the lower point with a clear gap. The exact shared B outer lower-sheet placement is retained. Hand, role, attachment and surface origin remain undetermined; no character or punctuation role is assigned.
Selected source attached; final root record approval pending.
Local component and candidate scopes retained exactly.
his hand for the ordinary writing; candidate-specific independent runs and separately identified local marks retain the undetermined-hand scopes printed in the component descriptions

Complete selected opening source, including every intervening word, formula, sign and owned graphical component. \deleted{Soit en effet}, with the single long cancellation rising across all three words; live Si on a follows outside the group. The wording and deletion are firm, his hand. Complete selected states in source order: \deleted{E}\Sigma_i^- with short head/retrace | \deleted{I}\Sigma_i^- with short head/retrace | \deleted{E}\Sigma_{\prime}^- with short head/retrace | \deleted{I}\Sigma_{\prime}^- with short head/retrace | \deleted{E}\Sigma_i^- with independent upper run | \deleted{I}\Sigma_i^- with independent upper run | \deleted{E}\Sigma_{\prime}^- with independent upper run | \deleted{I}\Sigma_{\prime}^- with independent upper run. E/i/head-retrace remains primary. The upright predecessor E/I, undotted short index i/prime and head/retrace versus independent-upper-run role keep their separate local scopes. Main writing is his hand; the independent-upper-run candidate alone retains undetermined hand for that run. The comma remains outside. This source group carries the first printed Sigma qualifier; predecessor confidence remains low. Complete selected states in source order: \deleted{=}\cap | \cap with unidentified crossed predecessor | \cap with two transverse retraces. The same two surviving transverse runs and live arch remain present in every complete state. The old-equals/predecessor/retrace allocation stays unresolved, his hand; the original C doubt remains low confidence. Barred U and the following E remain outside. Complete selected states in source order: E_i with detached top arm | E_j with detached top arm | E_i with independent upper curve | E_j with independent upper curve. The single high point and lower bent index remain within the complete E group once. i remains primary. Main E/index is his hand; only the independent-upper-curve candidate has undetermined upper-curve hand. The original C index doubt remains low confidence. \deleted{et si} followed by live alors. One long descending cancellation crosses both complete deleted words. The words and state are firm, his hand; alors remains outside the graphical group. Complete selected states in source order: on a | three reduced separate strokes without established lexical reading. The entire three-trace phrase stays in one qualified group. The on a candidate has his-hand attribution; the nonlexical-trace candidate retains undetermined hand, role and attachment.
